notes: The sheet bears manuscript page 39 in dark ink at the top and 79 in a lighter, pencil-like medium at the foot. The lower number is transcribed, but its authorship is not inferred. There is no date on the page.

The sheet gives two groupoid diagrams numbered (102) and (103), calls the lower arrow in (102) an equivalence of groupoids, and rewrites the configuration in (103). The horizontal label of (103) is overdrawn and remains uncertain.

The main paragraph compares the displayed phi map with the map on pi_1 for a fibration whose fibre is a product of punctured discs, or circles. It describes an extension by Z^C and defines C as the edges of underlined G, replacing the cancelled flèches with arêtes. These are page claims, not independently verified theorems in this reading.

The Attention note says to regard Z^C as a local system on the written pair, through the action of Gamma! on C. The NB note says the written base is a K(pi,1) and discusses an initial 1 in the homotopy exact sequence. No targeted proof check, independent re-proof, computation, or background theorem use was performed; check_events is therefore empty.

The original opening of the main paragraph is grammatically incomplete: after L'hom des groupoïdes phi, the next baseline starts propriétés. Following the main reader's prompt, I revisited the already saved header and removed the supplied a les in my initial draft. The dark mark and looped strokes to the right are part of the cancelled passage above, not a continuation of the main baseline. H's a comme is also absent.
Underlining of G is selective on this page. It is retained only where the separate bar is visible; ununderlined occurrences are not silently regularised from neighbouring formulas.

Quotation marks in the slanted caption and around extension are doubled raised strokes, rendered with two backticks and two apostrophes. The comma supplied by C after fondamentaux is not securely visible and is omitted in this draft pending main review.

The first callout has been integrated into the (102) tikz-cd composition, from the named equivalence label to its text. The long callout has been integrated into a TikZ composition containing the main Z^C label and the Attention note exactly once each. It points to Attention and merely crosses the NB writing.
